Part 2 · Wall thickness

How thick must vessels and pipes be, and is 36 barg enough for V-101?

Part 2 · the plan

From the code formula to a finding

  1. The shell ruleASME VIII-1 UG-27 and UG-32
  2. Worked: V-10136 barg gives a 38 mm plate
  3. Settle-outwhy 36 barg is not enough
  4. Pipe schedulesthe same rule, with mill tolerance

ASME VIII-1 · thin shell, inside radius, corroded

Hoop stress sets the shell; the head needs half

$$t=\frac{P\,R}{S\,E-0.6\,P}+CA,\qquad R=\frac{ID}{2}+CA,\qquad t_{head}=\frac{P\,D}{2\,S\,E-0.2\,P}+CA$$
$$MAWP=\frac{S\,E\,(t_n-CA)}{R+0.6\,(t_n-CA)}$$

Valid while $P\le0.385\,S\,E$; above it, thick-wall rules apply.

Worked example · V-101, DP 36 barg, ID 2500 mm step 1 of 2

The V-101 shell needs 36.2 mm

UG-27$t=PR/(SE-0.6P)+CA$
$R=1250+3=1253\ \text{mm}$corroded inside radius
$t=\dfrac{3.60\times1253}{138\times1-0.6\times3.60}=33.21\ \text{mm}$36 barg = 3.60 MPa
$33.21+3=36.21\ \text{mm}\ \rightarrow\ t_n=38\ \text{mm}$next standard plate

Worked example · V-101 step 2 of 2

The plate allows 37.9 barg

MAWP and head$MAWP=SE(t_n-CA)/(R+0.6(t_n-CA)),\quad t_{head}=PD/(2SE-0.2P)+CA$
$MAWP=\dfrac{138\times35}{1253+0.6\times35}=3.791\ \text{MPa}=37.9\ \text{barg}$corroded plate
$t_{head}=\dfrac{3.60\times2506}{276-0.72}+3=35.77\ \rightarrow\ 40\ \text{mm}$+10 % forming
$P_T\ge1.3\times36=46.8\ \text{barg}$hydrotest, UG-99

But is 36 barg the right pressure for V-101?

Interactive · pressure, diameter, part

Plate thickness grows almost linearly with P

UG-27$t=PR/(SE-0.6P)+CA$

For a 2.5 m shell, 36 → 80 barg takes the plate from 38 to 80 mm.

Interactive · pick the case before the trip (query EQ-ME-01)

After a trip, V-101 sees almost 70 barg

PSV-001 is upstream of ESDV-101 and cannot protect V-101: rate it 80 barg, 80 mm shell, ≈ 47 t.

Interactive · pick a line, change the pressure

Pipe uses the same rule, less 12.5 % mill tolerance

Pipe$t_{nom}\ge(PR/(SE-0.6P)+CA)/0.875$

All 14 lines pass at their system DP; DN500-PG-102 at 80 barg needs Sch 60.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • UG-27 gives V-101 a 38 mm shell at 36 barg, MAWP 37.9 barg.
  • Thickness rises almost linearly with pressure and diameter.
  • Settle-out 69.7 barg exceeds 36: rate V-101 for 80 barg.
  • Pipe schedules pass at their DP; PG-102 needs Sch 60 at 80 barg.

Part 3 · Sizing and rating

Are the scrubbers and coolers big enough, and what if a tube breaks?

Part 3 · the plan

From gas load to tube rupture

  1. ScrubbersSouders–Brown: which case sizes the vessel
  2. CoolersLMTD rating against the model's UA
  3. Tube rupturethe 10/13 rule fails twice
  4. Driver and pumpsGT-100 power and two pump duties

Scrubber sizing · vertical, mesh pad

Gas must rise slower than droplets fall

$$K=\frac{v_g}{\sqrt{(\rho_L-\rho_G)/\rho_G}},\qquad v_g=\frac{Q}{\pi D^2/4},\qquad D_{req}=\sqrt{\frac{4Q}{\pi\,v_{max}}}$$
$K$
Souders–Brown factor; limit 0.09 (derated mesh, Design tab)
m/s
$v_g,\ v_{max}$
gas velocity on the full section, its limit
m/s
$Q$
actual gas flow from the model
m³/s
$\rho_L,\ \rho_G$
liquid and gas density
kg/m³
$D$
vessel inside diameter
m

Interactive · vessel and diameter

The rated case, not the design case, sizes the scrubber

Souders–Brown$K=v_g\big/\sqrt{(\rho_L-\rho_G)/\rho_G}$

At 110 % K reaches 0.092 / 0.093: 2.6 m and 2.3 m would pass (EQ-ME-04).

Cooler rating · counter-current, gas in tubes

The duty over the mean driving force gives UA

$$\Delta T_{lm}=\frac{\Delta T_1-\Delta T_2}{\ln(\Delta T_1/\Delta T_2)},\qquad UA=\frac{Q}{\Delta T_{lm}}$$
$\Delta T_1$
gas in − cooling medium out (hot end)
K
$\Delta T_2$
gas out − cooling medium in (cold end)
K
$Q$
duty from the model run
kW
$UA$
required conductance, compared with the model's
kW/K

E-101 at design: 7302 kW over 18.4 K gives 397.6 kW/K; model 394.2.

Then the failure case: a tube breaks.

Interactive · cooler and case

At turndown the cooling-medium outlet moves, not the gas

Rating$UA=Q/\Delta T_{lm}$

LMTD and the model's ε-NTU agree within 1.2 %: one relation, two forms.

Interactive · tube rupture (API 521, query EQ-ME-02)

A 10 barg shell cannot take a broken 80 barg tube

10/13 rule$DP_{shell}\ge\tfrac{10}{13}\,DP_{tube}$

Hydrotest 1.3 × 10 = 13 barg: raise the shell to 61.5 / 106.2 barg, or relieve the rupture flow.

Rotating equipment · model numbers, pump duties assumed

GT-100 passes on a hot day, with little margin

GT-100

19.86 MW at 30 °C against 1.1 × 16.69 = 18.36 MW; 18.43 MW at 40 °C.

P-150A/B

Lube oil 49 m³/h at 5.5 bar, 15 kW each.

P-160

Both cooling valves open: 553 m³/h at 3.5 bar, 90 kW.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Scrubbers pass at design but not at 110 %: size at the rated case.
  • Cooler UA from LMTD matches the model within about 1 %.
  • Both coolers fail the 10/13 rule: a decision for Relief & vent.
  • GT-100 covers 1.1 × design shaft power at 30 °C.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Take design pressure from the system and its worst case, including settle-out.

2

Size plates with UG-27, then add corrosion allowance and round up.

3

Size scrubbers at the rated load, not the design point.

4

Check every exchanger's low-pressure side against the 10/13 rule.

5

Tag every datasheet number with its source.
